full_judgment:
2. Respondent No. 2 as the petitioner earlier filed an application on 3.9.84 under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act read with President's Order No. 88 of 1982 and President's Order No. 24 of 1972 for restoration of the mortgaged land comprising an area of .50 decimals before the Upazila Revenue Officer, Patiya, Chittagong against the petitioners and other heirs of late Abdus Samad Choudhury and that petition was registered as ML Case No. 5 of 1984-85. Their case is that the land originally belonged to respondent No. 2 and that one Yunus Mia, the predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos.16 to 21 was the attorney and nephew of late Abdus Samad Choudhury, the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner and respondent Nos. 3 to 12. Said Abdus Samad Choudhury was a Sub-Inspector of Police and was posted at Barisal and the said attorney and nephew used to manage his affairs and that on 13.12.1949 the said Yunus Mia purchased the scheduled land on behalf of Abdus Samad at a consideration of Taka 2,500 and got a deed in the benami of one Md. Ibrahim Miah, the predecessor of respondent Nos. 13 to 15 who was a close relation of said Abdus Samad Chowdhury and in the same sitting Md. Yunus Mia executed a deed of agreement to reconvey the land in question within three years to respondent No. 2 and that the case land was always in the possession of Abdus Samad Choudhury and after his death, his heirs namely, the present petitioners and respondent Nos. 3 to 12 possessed the same. It is also the case of the petitioners that ML Case was filed before the Upazila Revenue Officer, Chittgaong and that the said Yunus Mia died leaving behind respondent Nos.16 to 21 as his heirs and the said Ibrahim Mia died leaving behind respondent Nos. 13 to 15 who never possessed the land in question. It is also their case that transaction dated 13.12.49 was a mortgage and the petitioners along with respondent Nos.3 to 12 are bound to restore the case land to respondent No.2. After the case was registered before the Upazila Revenue Officer as ML Case No. 5 of 1984-85 notices were issued upon the present petitioners and respondents No. 3 to 21 and petitioner No.1 on receipt of the same filed a written objection on 24.10.84 stating, inter alia, that Md. Yunus Mia was never the attorney of late Abdus Samad Choudhury and neither the said predecessor nor the petitioners are bound by his acts and deeds and the said Yunus Mia was never authorised by any power of attorney, registered or otherwise, to act on behalf of Abdus Samad Choudhury and that the alleged transaction dated 13.12.49 took place long before the promulgation and operation of section. 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and President's Order No. 88 of 1972 and President's Order 24 of 1973 and the same does not come within the mischief of that section. Their further case is that Chapter V of the said Acquisition Act which contained section 95A of the Act came into operation in the District of Chittagong on 1.8.63 by Notification No. SR 116-63-609 dated 18.7.1963 while sub-section 1 of section 95 was amended by EP Ordinance XXI of 1969 on 18.11.1969 and the alleged transaction which took place under the Bengal Tenancy Act was repealed with effect from 1.8.63 and, as such, respondent No.2 was not entitled to any relief as prayed for in the aforesaid ML Case. Their further case is that section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Ac which came into operation in 1972 covers an out and out sale with an agreement for reconveyance to be treated as complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding 7 years and that the instant transaction is an out and out sale and even assuming that there is an agreement, seven years period having been elapsed long before the promulgation of President's Order No.88 of 1972 the transaction is past and closed and beyond the jurisdiction of any Revenue Officer authorised for that purpose. The matter was heard by the Upazila Revenue Officer, Patiya, Chittagong who by his judgment and order dated 10.4.85 allowed the restoration of the mortgaged land The petitioners then moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 3. Mr. S R Pal, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners, at the very outset submits that the transaction dated 13.12.1949 is out and out a sale and the purchaser never entered into any agreement with the vendor for reconveyance of the purchased land and he has also not authorised Yunus Mia to execute any agreement on his behalf. He submits that the facts and circumstance indicated that the transaction is out and out a sale and can never be construed as an usufructuary mortgage. He also submits that the transaction dated 13.12.49 is past and closed on the date of promulgation of President's Order 88/72 and respondent No. 1, the Upazila Revenue Officer acted without jurisdiction in allowing the application of respondent No. 2 treating the transaction as usufructuary mortgage. He submits that the said transaction governed by the Transfer of Property Act and the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act having no retrospective effect in the facts and circumstances of the case the same was wrongly applied in the present case before us. He further submits that in view of the provisions of law any transfer of a holding or part thereof by a raiyat by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for period of maximum seven years and in the facts and circumstances of the instant case as the alleged transaction of 13.12.49 is not subsisting on the day of promulgation of President's Order No. 88 of 1972, Respondent No. 1 acted illegally and without jurisdiction in allowing the application because the alleged transaction was not alive on the date of the promulgation of the aforesaid President's Order and the transaction is very much past and closed. 

 4. Mvi. Mohammad Wahidullah, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 2, submits that the transaction dated 13.12.49 is nothing but a complete usufructuary mortgage as Yunus Mia was the authorised agent of the purchaser and he paid the money to the vendor on his behalf and he himself executed and registered a deed of agreement on the same date. He argued that the conduct of the parties at the relevant time indicate that the transaction is a complete usufructuary mortgage and as it is a complete usufructuary mortgage the Upazila Revenue Officer rightly allowed the case under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 5. Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was incorporated in the said Act by President's Order 88 of 1972 and it runs as follows: 

 "95A. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any transfer of a holding or of a portion or share thereof, either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey, or where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess, and to enjoy the usufruct of, such holding or portion or share thereof for a specified period of time in lieu of such consideration, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provisions of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Amendment) Order, 1972 (president's Order No. 88 of 1972)." 

 6. In the back-drop of the provision of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, let us examine the deed dated 13.12.1949 and also the deed of agreement executed and registered on that date. The deed of transfer dated 13.12.1949 is annexed to the petition as Annexure-B. We have carefully gone through the deed and it appears to us that one Mohammad Abdus Salam sold the land described in the schedule attached to this deed at a consideration of Taka 2,500.00 to one Md. Ibrahim Mia and the vendor received the consideration money through Md. Yunus Mia who is a relation of said Mvi. Ibrahim Mia. From a recital of Annexure-B it appears that it is an out and out sale deed. Now to make it a complete usufructuary mortgage something more is required to be done and that is an agreement to reconvey this land as provided under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It is the definite case of the respondents that on 13.12.1949 a deed of agreement was executed and registered on behalf of said Mvi. Ibrahim Mia by his attorney Md. Yunus Mia who is a close relation of said Ibrahim Mia. A copy of this agreement is annexed to the petition as Annexure-C. We have carefully gone through Annexure-C and it appears that on 13.12.1949 the said Yunus Mia executed and registered a deed of agreement for reconveyance wherein he promised to get the land reconveyed to said Abdus Salam on his receiving Taka 2,500.00 (which is the consideration money of the aforesaid sale deed) within 3 years from 13.12.1949. It is the definite case of the respondent that this agreement made the said transaction a complete usufructuary mortgage. We have already found that the transaction dated 13.12.1949 is out and out a sale and now to make it a mortgage it must be found that Annexure-C is a valid agreement as required under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. From this Annexure-C it appears that the said Yunus Mia while executing and registering this Annexure-C has not styled himself as a constituted attorney of Mvi. Ibrahim Mia who purchased the disputed land. Nowhere in Annexure-C he mentioned that he acted on behalf of Mvi. Ibrahim Mia or that he acted as constituted attorney of Md. Ibrahim Mia, the vendee of the land in question. From the recital of Annexure-C it appears that Md. Yunus Mia promised that on receipt of consideration of Taka 2,500.00 he will get the mortgage redeemed and he will also get the land transferred to the vendor. It appears that this is a promise by one Yunus Mia who had no power of attorney on behalf of said Ibrahim Mia who purchased the land from Md. Abdus Salam. In such a case of mortgage the agreement to reconvey must have been executed and registered by the purchaser himself or at best by his attorney constituted for that purpose and unless that is done, an agreement by a third party cannot be constituted as an agreement as provided under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. After consideration of Annexures B & C, we are of the view that this Annexure-C has not in any way made Annexure-D a complete usufructuary mortgage as required under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Furthermore, before executing Annexure-C, the vendee ought to have appointed said Yunus Mia as his constituted attorney and when a land is in question the power of attorney ought to have been registered which is very much lacking in the present case before us. Thus after considering these two Annexures we hold that Annexure-B is nothing but an out and out sale deed and by Annexure-C the same has not been made a usufructuary mortgage to attract section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 7. It appears that Annexure-B was executed and registered on 13.12.1949. Now assuming for argument's sake that this annexure-B is a complete usufructuary mortgage where the provision of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is applicable. Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is in Part V of the aforesaid Act and this Part V of the said Act came into operation in the District of Chittagong on 1st August, 1963. The principle of law on the effectiveness of Part V of the Act is well settled in the case of Abdul Mannan & others vs. Kuloda Ranjan Mowali & others, reported in 31 DLR (AD) 195. The Appellate Division observed in that case that the retrospectivity of the provision of sub-section (2) of section 87 cannot be pushed beyond the date of commencement of Part V of the Act in the area where the accretion in question has taken place. Following this principle of law we hold that Part V of the said Act came into effect from 1.8.1963 and the provisions of section 95A which is within the Part V of the said Act cannot be pushed beyond 1.8.1963. Admittedly this transaction is dated 13.12.1949 and even if we take this transaction as complete usufructuary mortgage this cannot be redeemed under section 95A of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act when on the date of coming into effect of Part V in Chittagong, the period of 7 years had already elapsed and, as such, the transaction is past and closed. Furthermore, from 1.8.1963 the Bengal Tenancy Act has been repealed in Chittagong. The transaction in question took place under the aforesaid Bengal Tenancy Act and the said Act was repealed on 1.8.1963 which is beyond the period as provided in Annexure-C and after the promulgation of President's Order 88 of 1972 the petition for redemption of mortgage as made out by the petitioner in the aforesaid case cannot be entertained as the matter has already became past and closed. 

 9. We have thoroughly considered materials on record particularly Annexures-B and C and we hold that Annexure-B is out and out a sale without any condition for reconveyance and the same cannot be construed as a complete usufructuary mortgage. The Upazila Revenue Officer illegally applied section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and it requires interference by this Court. We hold that the transaction is out and out a sale and section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has no manner of application in the present case before us.
